clue.text: Underground shelter for trapped clubmen

definitions.meaning: a reinforced dugout where people take cover from bombs
a golf sand trap that catches players carrying clubs

explanation.surface: A refuge below ground offered to members of a club who are stuck somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubmen' sounds like members of a gentlemen's club, but they are golfers wielding clubs, caught in a sand hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a military dugout and a sandy hazard on a golf course.

clue.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

definitions.text: He suffers from a lack of balance

parts.words: He suffers from a lack of balance
parts.note: the balance is money in a bank account, not physical steadiness

explanation.surface: A man who keeps falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests steadiness on one's feet; it is a bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insolvent has no funds left to pay debts.

clue.text: Insect that is dissected gives precise details

indicators.note: dissected means cut apart, so the letters are taken to pieces and reassembled

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Cutting up a bug reveals fine points of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine distinctions or exact points of detail are subtleties.

clue.text: Jacob supplanted him in the wages audit

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the phrase wages audit

explanation.surface: Jacob replaced someone during a pay inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob took his twin brother's birthright and blessing.

clue.text: Spoil beautiful Italian holiday resort

parts.note: to spoil something is to mar it
bella is the Italian word for beautiful

explanation.surface: A lovely Italian woman ruins a seaside break.
explanation.walkthrough: Marbella is a Spanish resort on the Costa del Sol, so 'Italian' belongs to the wordplay, not the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known Spanish coastal town much visited by sun-seeking tourists.

clue.text: Not even a gymnast would use such bars

definitions.text: a gymnast would use such bars
definitions.meaning: women's gymnastics uses uneven bars set at two heights

explanation.surface: A gymnast's bars are lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking symmetry means uneven, and the uneven bars are a gymnastics apparatus.

clue.text: Clip round the ear — or waist

definitions.meaning: a smack on the head, a hard blow
a strap worn round the waist

explanation.surface: Choosing where to hit someone, the head or the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'clip round the ear' is British slang for a cuff to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a hard blow; the other is the strap worn about the middle.

clue.text: Pound added by university fellow to the capital

parts.note: L is the pound sign, from Latin libra
on can mean in addition, added
a don is a university lecturer or fellow

explanation.surface: A university fellow sends money to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The British capital city, seat of government.

clue.text: A fool it's silly to help

parts.note: a fool is an ass

indicators.note: silly says the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fool declares that helping is daft.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid or support someone.

clue.text: Drink specially made for the Olympics

definitions.text: Drink specially made for the Olympics

parts.words: Drink specially made for the Olympics
parts.note: the Olympics here are the gods of Mount Olympus, whose drink in Greek myth was a divine beverage

explanation.surface: An official sports drink brewed for the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: The Olympics suggest the Games, but they are the Olympian gods of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology the gods on Olympus drank this along with eating ambrosia.

clue.text: Rides round on whirlwinds

indicators.note: round says the word for rides goes about the next word

parts.note: rides a bicycle, that is cycles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes cycling through violent winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating storms are the classic swirling, destructive winds.

clue.text: Gate-crasher?

parts.note: not an uninvited party guest but a siege weapon that smashes gates

explanation.walkthrough: A gatecrasher is normally an uninvited guest; here it literally crashes through gates.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy beam swung against castle gates to break them down.

clue.text: List of Biblical books held by academy

indicators.note: held by says the books sit inside the academy's letters

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An academy keeps a catalogue of books from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule or roster listing whose turn it is.

clue.text: Sounding more relaxed with one's destiny

indicators.note: Sounding says the word is heard rather than written, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: more relaxed means calmer

explanation.surface: Someone becomes calmer once they accept their fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The likeness works in a British accent where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist belief the force of one's deeds shapes fate, hence destiny.

clue.text: An outstanding manager

definitions.meaning: a knob or stud that stands out, as on a shield or ceiling
the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent but means literally projecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary ones: a raised ornamental knob and a person who runs things.

clue.text: Exclude from French drinking place

parts.note: de is French for from
a bar is a place for drinking

explanation.surface: Someone is banned from a French pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar or prohibit someone from something.

clue.text: Instant tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Choosing between instant tea and instant coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like a kind of drink but means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine coffee named after the Yemeni port, often mixed with chocolate.

clue.text: Nearest point at sea for the launch

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat launched as close as possible to the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A product launch is its formal unveiling or showing to the public.

clue.text: Gold in finals' round? Quite the opposite, producing serious complaint

indicators.note: in would put the gold inside the jumbled word
Quite the opposite reverses the container, so gold goes outside instead

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: round means the letters of finals are spun about

explanation.surface: A sporting final goes wrong, causing an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'Gold in' would bury the gold; 'Quite the opposite' flips that, so the gold wraps the scrambled word instead ('round' makes SIANFL).
explanation.definitionFit: An influenza pandemic, notably of 1957, was a serious illness.

clue.text: Beaten by an heroic exploit in action

indicators.note: in says the exploit goes inside the action

parts.note: a deed is an action
a feat is a heroic exploit

explanation.surface: Someone loses to a bold heroic act.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defeated means being beaten or overcome.

clue.text: It's said to be one way to ensure a good stretch of repentance

definitions.text: It's said to be one way to ensure a good stretch of repentance

parts.words: It's said to be one way to ensure a good stretch of repentance
parts.note: the proverb warns that a hurried wedding leads to regret at leisure

explanation.surface: Folk wisdom about how to guarantee a long spell of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's first half: rushing into a wedding means repenting at leisure.

clue.text: Intimidates the French, surrounded by weapons

indicators.note: surrounded by says the article sits inside the weapons

parts.note: arms are weapons
la is French for the

explanation.surface: French people are menaced by guns all around.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm is to frighten or intimidate.

clue.text: Having clinched the deal shut up!

definitions.meaning: sealed or concluded, as a sale

explanation.surface: A negotiator tells the other side to be quiet once the agreement is signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up!' looks like an order to be quiet but means simply shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal concluded is finished; a shop shut is not open.

clue.text: Quiet university, three students seen around

indicators.note: seen around says the students' letters surround the university's

parts.note: L stands for learner, a student driver; three of them give three Ls

explanation.surface: A university is peaceful with only three students on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A lull is a calm, quiet spell in activity.

clue.text: Require sound massage

indicators.note: sound says the word for require is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to require is to need

explanation.surface: Someone badly wants a proper rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To work dough or muscles with the hands is to massage them.

clue.text: Mean to be bottom

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is ignoble or low; the other is the foundation something rests on.

clue.text: Some of them may be featured in Austen novel

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of these people could appear in a Jane Austen book.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'be featured in'; that phrase is a link word, since 'Austen novel' alone defines the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1815 work about a matchmaking heroine is titled with her name.

clue.text: A natural hanger-on, in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: a prickly seed head that clings to fur and clothing
a rolled R accent, as in some Scottish or West Country speech

explanation.surface: A clingy person, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanger-on' suggests a sycophant; it is a sticky seed pod from nature.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a clinging seed case; the other is a regional accent with rolled Rs.

clue.text: She makes me turn in a string of beads

indicators.note: in says the flipped word goes inside the beads

parts.note: a rosary is a string of prayer beads

indicators.note: turn says the word me is flipped round

explanation.surface: A woman makes the speaker spin around inside a bead necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a fair definition because the answer is a woman's name; 'turn' makes EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a female first name, so 'She' stands for a woman so called.

clue.text: Not in suitable attire

parts.note: not in means out
suitable means fit

explanation.surface: Someone is not wearing the right clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, synonymous with dress.

clue.text: Weapons carried personally by team members

parts.note: a team is a side
limbs such as arms are members of the body

explanation.surface: Players on a team each carry their own guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' reads as team-mates but means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords worn at the hip are weapons kept on one's person.

clue.text: Approximately three minutes in the ring

definitions.meaning: a single boxing session lasts three minutes

explanation.surface: Roughly the length of a boxing bout's session.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as A ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Around means about; a round in boxing lasts three minutes.
